new.n: Shiawassee County's first fair ground, Corunna (1850-1858)
new.pl: A whole block lettered 'Fair Ground' in Castle's Addition, south of David St and north of King St, two blocks east of the river loop (1859 county map inset)
new.v: Fairground coin and token drops from 19th-century county fairs
new.st: The 1880 county history says the first Shiawassee County fairs, 1850-58, were held 'on grounds situated on the south side of the river, prepared by the citizens'. The 1859 Geil & Jones map's Corunna Village inset letters a whole block 'Fair Ground' in Castle's Addition, south of David Street and north of King Street. The pin was moved onto the 1926 USGS sheet using the river loop and the Shiawassee Street crossing, and that sheet shows open ground there.
new.t: Today's use not yet checked; look-only if built over. Otherwise ask the landowner. Gathering grounds: under the oldest trees, the flat where the crowd stood, the track edges and where wagons parked.
src: Geil & Jones, Map of Genesee and Shiawassee Counties, Michigan (1859), Corunna Village inset (Library of Congress 2011588008)
pinev: 1859 inset block moved onto the 1926 USGS sheet by the river loop and Shiawassee St crossing; about 200 m
new.tovw: Lead grade C (early Michigan fairgrounds thread)
